verdict.rationale: Sumsub documents a first-party Sandbox mode for testing an integration before going live, covering app tokens, webhooks, and the WebSDK. The docs say it covers only "most" of Sumsub's functionality, and none of the cited text states that sandbox data is isolated from production. missing for 10: explicit documentation that sandbox data is separated from production, a definition of which features are excluded from sandbox, guidance on agent/MCP use against sandbox, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: Use Sandbox mode to test your integration before going live.
Sandbox lets you access most of the Sumsub functionality so that you can: Set up and test your integration using app tokens, webhooks, and our WebSDK.
